newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent falls in thin trade, Iraqi news pressure.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent falls in thin trade, Iraqi news pressure.

text.p: IPE Brent futures fell sharply in thin early trade on Monday as the market corrected following last week's rally and news of imminent Iraqi oil exports pressured the market slightly, brokers said.
"It's basically taking a breather after last week's rise," said one trader.
January Brent was trading 50 cents lower at $24.04 a barrel at 1100 GMT, while December gas oil was trading $3.25 a tonne lower at $220.50.
Traders said news that the first Iraqi oil exports in six years were imminent was pressuring the market slightly, but most added the news had already been priced into the market to a great extent.
"It's pressuring the market a bit," said another trader.
"But the return of Iraqi oil has been discounted to a great extent I think what we're seeing is some corrective activity after last week's rally.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said on Friday that Iraq expected to be able to resume oil exports from 0500 GMT on Tuesday.
